risks.description: The approval endpoint hangs and never responds; every approval POST observed in this run timed out, so approvals cannot be recorded at all.
risks.basis: Clusters C01-C04: POST /api/invoices/*/approve all 'got timed out'

risks.description: A timed-out approval request may or may not have durably recorded the approval, leaving an ambiguous/partial persisted state that no observer can trust.
risks.basis: C01-C04 timeouts + AC-APPROVAL-001 requires the approval be recorded durably

risks.description: Two concurrent approvals of the same invoice could double-record or corrupt the durable approval state.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 durable single record; gen-idempotent covered only sequential double-call

risks.description: Approval state may not survive an api process restart, violating the promise that persisted state survives a re-read.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-002 approval state survives a re-read of persisted state

risks.description: Approving an unknown invoice or sending a malformed body may hang or silently write junk instead of being cleanly rejected without persisting.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 records approving an invoice; unknown/garbage input must not create durable records

scenarios.title: Approval of SMOKE survives an api restart and re-read
scenarios.purpose: Prove that a recorded approval is durable across a process restart and can be re-read afterward, which is the literal promise of AC-APPROVAL-002.
scenarios.rationale: Restarting api is the strongest test of 'survives a re-read of persisted state'; no other covered scenario cycles the process.
setup: Ensure api is running on http://127.0.0.1:8959
expected_observations: state.py SMOKE reports approved before restart
state.py SMOKE still reports approved after api restart
forbidden_observations: approval for SMOKE absent after restart
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses the single fixed SMOKE key; approving SMOKE is idempotent, so re-running does not accumulate distinct records. Runs alone under isolation_key api-service because it restarts the shared api process.

scenarios.title: Retrying an approve after a timeout records exactly one durable approval
scenarios.purpose: Given every approve currently times out, verify that a client retry does not double-record; the durable state must show a single approval regardless of how many times the timed-out call was retried.
scenarios.rationale: The observed failure mode is timeouts; a real client will retry, so exactly-once durability under retry is the load-bearing worry.
expected_observations: W2A appears approved exactly once in persisted state
forbidden_observations: W2A recorded as approved more than once
persisted state for W2A is corrupt or malformed
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses a unique invoice id W2A not shared with any other scenario, so its writes cannot contaminate others; no reset command is approved, so isolation relies on id uniqueness.

scenarios.title: A timed-out approve does not leave ambiguous half-written state
scenarios.purpose: When the approve call times out under a tight deadline, the persisted store must be internally consistent: either W2B is fully approved or it is absent, never a partial/corrupt record.
scenarios.rationale: AC-001 demands durability; a timeout that leaves a torn record would make the durable state untrustworthy.
expected_observations: state.py exits cleanly and reports W2B as either approved or not present, with well-formed output
forbidden_observations: state.py reports a corrupt/partial record for W2B
state reader errors out reading W2B
scenarios.isolation_note: Unique invoice id W2B used only here; id uniqueness prevents contamination since no reset command is approved.

scenarios.title: Two simultaneous approvals of one invoice record a single durable approval
scenarios.purpose: Exercise a race the sequential idempotency test cannot: fire two approvals for W2C at the same instant and confirm the durable store holds exactly one approval.
scenarios.rationale: gen-idempotent-approve was sequential; concurrent writes can interleave and double-record or corrupt state in ways a sequential call never triggers.
expected_observations: W2C is approved exactly once after two concurrent approvals
forbidden_observations: persisted state for W2C corrupted by the race
scenarios.isolation_note: Unique invoice id W2C used only by this scenario; must not run concurrently with anything else touching W2C (isolation_key invoice:W2C).

scenarios.title: Approving an unknown invoice is rejected and records nothing
scenarios.purpose: An approve for a nonexistent invoice id must be cleanly rejected (not hang) and must not create a durable approval record.
scenarios.rationale: AC-001 records approval of an invoice; a bogus id must not manufacture a durable record, and given the hang cluster it must also respond rather than time out.
expected_observations: Approve for unknown invoice returns a client error within 6s
no approved record exists for W2D-UNKNOWN
forbidden_observations: a durable approval is created for the unknown invoice
scenarios.isolation_note: Reads/writes only the unknown id W2D-UNKNOWN, which no other scenario references; a rejected request should write nothing at all.

scenarios.title: Malformed approve body is rejected without persisting
scenarios.purpose: A syntactically malformed request body must be rejected cleanly (no hang) and must not write a durable approval for W2E.
scenarios.rationale: Durable records should only result from valid approvals; malformed input must not corrupt or populate the store.
expected_observations: malformed body rejected with a 4xx within 6s
no approved record exists for W2E
forbidden_observations: malformed input produces a durable approval or corrupts state
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses unique id W2E only; a rejected malformed request should persist nothing, so it cannot contaminate later scenarios.

unresolved_questions: Neither acceptance criterion states who is authorized to approve an invoice, so authorization/cross_tenant scenarios cannot be grounded — confirm whether approval must be access-controlled before verifying it.

The ACs do not define the required response shape or status code for a successful approval beyond 'records durably'; the 200 expectations above are assumed and should be confirmed against the intended contract.

No approved command resets persisted approval state, so scenarios rely on unique invoice ids for isolation rather than teardown — confirm whether a reset/cleanup mechanism should exist for the durable store.
